ResearchProjectDef.label: weather lore
ResearchProjectDef.description: Where lightning falls and why: the tall, the metal, the wet. A pole of any metal, set in the ground, takes the sky's strikes near it and sends them down into the earth.

ResearchProjectDef.label: keepers of the weather
ResearchProjectDef.description: The weather lore carried into the stream: an altar where casters talk the sky round - rain and fog, the wind raised or stilled, clouds driven off, and, for a circle of mages, the storm itself.

ThingDef.label: lightning rod
ThingDef.description: A pole of metal set deep in the ground. Every lightning strike of the sky within nine cells goes into it and down into the earth - nothing runs on to the wires, the batteries or the people near. Switched "into the grid" and touching a power line, it sends the strikes to the batteries instead; what they cannot take goes into the ground. It must stand under the open sky.
